mcqs.q: A price increases by 20% then decreases by 20%. Is the final price the same as the original?
options: No — the final price is 96% of the original (a 4% net decrease), because each percentage is applied to a different base.
Simple interest grows faster than compound because it has fewer steps.
Yes — a 20% rise and a 20% fall cancel out exactly.
Yes — percentage changes always cancel because they are symmetric.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
options: Simple and compound interest give the same total — compound just uses a different formula.
Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount; compound interest is calculated on the original amount plus accumulated interest.
Yes — percentage changes always cancel because they are symmetric.
Simple interest grows faster than compound because it has fewer steps.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
The square root of x (the positive root when x is positive).
Yes — percentage changes always cancel because they are symmetric.
x^(1/2) means x divided by 2 — half of x.
